properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, AND NOT LEGAL ADVICE. Anthony, 2026-09-23: keep reflow2 open for the public to use; the brothers are building flo2.io to make money; others must not build products on reflow2 that compete with flo2.io, or use it for profit.

⭐ THE KEY FACT: Apache-2.0 (today's license) permits ALL of that — commercial use, competing products, closed derivatives. What he wants is a SOURCE-AVAILABLE license: public can read, run and modify, with commercial/competitive limits. None of these is "open source" by the OSI definition, which matters for some adopters.

IDEAS, NONE CHOSEN — the named licenses closest to what he said:
(a) POLYFORM SHIELD 1.0.0 — any use EXCEPT providing a product that competes with the licensor's products. The closest single match to "don't compete with flo2.io". Counter: "competes" is judged against what the licensor offers, so flo2.io's scope decides its reach.
(b) FUNCTIONAL SOURCE LICENSE (FSL) — any "permitted purpose" except competing use; each release automatically becomes Apache-2.0/MIT two years later. Popular (Sentry) and simple. Counter: the two-year conversion means old versions become fully free.
(c) BUSINESS SOURCE LICENSE (BSL 1.1) — source-available with an "Additional Use Grant" you write (e.g. "any use except a competing offering"), converting to open source after up to four years. Flexible, well-known (HashiCorp, MariaDB). Counter: the grant is custom text you must word well.
(d) POLYFORM NONCOMMERCIAL 1.0.0 — no commercial use at all without a separate paid license. Matches "can't use reflow2 for profit" and the brother's July idea (free for personal/school, paid for business). Counter: it forbids ALL commercial use, even a company using reflow2 internally for its own designs, which may be broader than he wants — and it expressly allows government use for free.
(e) ELASTIC LICENSE 2.0 — anyone may use it except offering it as a hosted/managed service or circumventing license keys. Aimed at cloud resellers; narrower than "no competing product".
(f) DUAL LICENSING — a restrictive public license plus a paid commercial license the owners sell. Requires the owners to hold (or be licensed) all the rights — which is why the ownership question comes first.

⚠️ WHAT CANNOT BE UNDONE: versions already published under Apache-2.0 stay Apache-2.0 for anyone who has them. A new license binds future versions. With 0 forks today the practical exposure is small — but it grows with every release under Apache.
properties.name: OPEN — which license keeps reflow2 free for the public to use while stopping anyone building a product on it that competes with flo2.io?
properties.no_relation_note: No graph node on reflow2's license existed before this session; the July note lives only in machine-local memory. Related to its sibling ideas recorded in the same session, linked separately.
properties.rationale: One question per decision: which license, separate from who owns it and from forks. The options are the source-available licenses whose published text comes closest to his words; a lawyer should confirm the fit, especially how "competes with flo2.io" is defined.
